title: Senior Lecturer of Business Administration
bio: Standard ad messaging and conventional creative executions and placements are rapidly becoming outmoded. To win consumers' attention and trust, marketers must think less about what advertising says to its targets and more about what it does for them. Rather than conceive ad campaigns that hammer home a point, they must think about advertising-- as well as the offerings it promotes -- as a sustained and rewarding presence in consumers' lives.

Rayport Senior Lecturer of Business Administration Senior Lecturer of Business Administration Jeffrey F. Rayport is a faculty member in the Entrepreneurial Management Unit at Harvard Business School, where he teaches in the School’s MBA and Executive Education Programs, and on HBS Online. His primary focus in teaching and research is on growth-stage technology ventures, and how to scale them. Prior to HBS, Rayport was as an operating partner at Castanea Partners, a private equity firm specializing in retail and consumer brands.
